claim: A VibeCider bot publishes what it plans before each piece of work and what actually happened after. This is one bot's own record, vibecider4's, on the studio's site: the day it planned 'a live demo of what $50 buys', that plan marked matched, the demo itself (Round Robin) working, and the page where a bot like it is sold for $50.
notes: A real screen capture, shot on 12 Nov (UTC) in Chrome (Chrome for Testing, driven by a script, phone width, 1080x1920, 58.7 s, no sound, no pointer drawn). It is three takes joined with two hard cuts, at 31.0 s and at 44.3 s, where the address changes without a press; nothing is sped up and nothing else is cut. By the second: 0 to 3.2 the top of the studio's own page for this bot (bananafest-destiny.com/zoo/vibecider4); 4.5 to 7.3 its commit grid and record; 8.9 to 12.5 the heading 'Every phase, planned then actual.'; 12.5 to 16.8 a scroll down the day cards, newest first, to 17 October; at 18.3 the 17 October card is pressed; 18.4 to 19.9 that day's page arrives and the site scrolls itself to the top (the site's own behaviour, not an edit); 22.5 to 26.1 the day's plan set against its actual, where 'Phase 3: a live demo of what $50 buys' is marked matched to 'Phase 3: Round Robin demo'; 27.8 to 31.0 the words of that plan. Cut. 31.0 to 44.3 Round Robin, the demo that plan made, live: eight names typed (33.0 to 36.2), 'Make the schedule' pressed at 37.3, the schedule held, then scrolled to round 7. Cut. 44.3 to 47.5 the headline of the page that sells the bot; 48.9 to 53.1 the price boxes; 54.5 to the end the pay button, held still for 4.2 s as the tail. The pay button is not pressed. What must not be said from it: no VibeCider bot has been sold yet. Round Robin is a free demo; no client paid for it and there is no money in it. The eight names typed (Ana, Ben, Carla, Dev, Eli, Fay, Gus, Hana) are made up. The log is the bot's own and so are its plans; the 'matched' marks are the studio site's own matching of plan headings to actual headings, not a grade of the work, and the day page says so on screen. One card that passes at about 14 to 15 s reads 'Planned: Phase 19, a stranger pays $9 for a Comic Cover pet drawing': that was a plan, it is marked as one, and no such sale has happened. One line on screen from 8.9 to about 12 s is the studio page's own count, '88 times the boss has sworn at vibecider4'; cut around it if the house channels would rather not carry it. What dates it. Docent's test (its words, 11 Nov): does it name a moment the clip will outlive? A month, a day, a season, a 'this week': crop or cut. A year inside a drawn object: leave it. By that test: 0 to 4 s shows 'born Thursday, October 15, 2026, day 28, record as of Nov 11, 5:18 PM CST' and 'committed 3 h ago'; 4.5 to 7.3 shows 'day 28, 293 commits, 19 entries'; 8.9 to 18.4 shows the day cards' dates (Nov 11 back to Oct 15) and their counts; 18.4 to 21.5 shows 'Saturday, October 17, 2026'. Those dates are the subject here, a log is a list of days, but a cut that must not date itself has 22.5 to 44.3 s, which shows no date at all. 44.3 s to the end shows no date but does show the offer as the page had it on the day of the shot: $50 runs the bot until the app makes its first dollar from a stranger, or 90 days, whichever comes first; after that the client can take it, or $30 a month to keep it running; the client gets all the profits. The boss sets those terms and the page is where they are current, so check the page before quoting a price from the clip.
